text:
elaine: FYI ran into flaky auth during onboarding lab. different sample apps and SDKs use different env var names (REDWOOD_API_KEY vs RW_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_TOKEN). new hires copy/paste and hit 401s. :grimacing:
rob: ugh. is it just names or scope precedence too?
elaine: both. go SDK assumes org-scoped keys first, python prefers project-scoped first, node falls back to account-only.
toni: that's a parity bug. we should decide a canonical precedence and enforce in SDKs. my vote: project -> org -> account. matches how customers grant narrowest scope by default.
rob: agreed. also we need a rotation story: ops uses short-lived secrets in CI and our SDKs currently read env on startup and never refresh. saw nightly e2e fail after token expiry.
elaine: yeah the job died mid-run. no transparent refresh path.
sdk-bot: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/501  Align env var names + add pluggable credential provider (created by sdk-bot)
toni: design idea: SDKs accept an optional credentialProvider (sync or async) that returns { token, expiresAt }. SDKs should call provider at init, and on 401 call provider once and retry. keep retry-to-once to avoid loops.
rob: provider pattern makes sense. also add small official helpers for AWS/GCP secret fetch so sample apps can show best practices.
elaine: short-term mitigation: SDKs should accept legacy env names as fallbacks but log a single-process deprecation warning when they are present. update all sample apps to canonical REDWOOD_API_KEY + REDWOOD_SCOPE.
toni: devex lint idea: add a pre-commit or release pipeline check that scans sample repos for non-canonical env names and fails CI with a helpful message including sed replacement.
ops-bot: ops request: support env-based provider discovery for containerized workloads. if REDWOOD_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER=auto then SDK should attempt a well-known local endpoint before env/static key.
elaine: hmm prefer explicit over magic. can document auto discovery but keep default simple: env key first, then provider.
rob: agree. let's document clear precedence: 1) explicit env key (REDWOOD_API_KEY), 2) credentialProvider callback, 3) legacy fallbacks (log deprecation).
toni: timeline proposal: quick PRs to add fallback+deprecation logs in 1 week, update sample apps + lint in 2 weeks, credentialProvider implementation + helpers in 4 weeks, cross-SDK parity check in 6 weeks. deprecate legacy names after 6 months.
elaine: I'll open the sample-app PRs today to switch to REDWOOD_API_KEY and add README note about REDWOOD_SCOPE. rob can own SDK lint rule.
rob: taking lint. will also draft the provider API spec for parity (simple surface: getToken() => {token, expiresAt}).
ops-bot: note recorded: ops will test provider flow with short-lived tokens in staging once SDK PRs land.
toni: one more: SDKs should emit structured logs when a 401 triggers provider refresh so we can correlate failed requests in production. minimal fields: attempt, provider_used (bool), request_id.
elaine: good call. I'll add that to the PR. pinging @devex for thumbs on naming: REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_SCOPE.
rob: thumbs up from me.
toni: +1.
elaine: thanks folks  I'll post PR links here when ready.
